question: RQ2: cache economics of compression — invalidation model, placement, batching, break-even

setup.host: isolated DSH 0.1.0-rc.7 web profile, ARC 0.2.0-beta.4, scnet/GLM-5.2
setup.arcConfig: modelContextLimit 32768, autoNudge false, governor disabled (profile user patch)
setup.plantVolume: ~26K projected tokens per arm, 4 plant turns + settle turns
setup.rounds: round1 baseline/head/middle/batch/sequent; round2 head/batch (neutral summary text); round3 batch2/sequent2 controls

invalidateModel.finding: Prefix caching invalidates from the FIRST CHANGED MESSAGE, not from the shadowed content: the summary node lands at the compression point and the entire tail after it re-enters uncached input on the next call.

headCompress.interpretation: compressing the OLDEST turn re-caches nearly the whole session tail

middleCompress.interpretation: compressing a MIDDLE turn re-caches only the tail after it

noCompressionSteadyState.interpretation: prefix caching otherwise absorbs growth: ~101 uncached tokens per call (mean of the last four pre-compression calls)

invalidateModel.hypothesisVerdict: HYPOTHESIS (a) FALSIFIED IN DIRECTION: oldest-first placement MAXIMIZES re-cache cost; the cache-optimal placement is the newest compressible range (just outside the protected zone). Semantic oldest-first preference and cache cost are in tension.

batching.finding: One batched compress call produces ONE invalidation event; sequential compressions pay the tail re-write repeatedly.
batching.hypothesisVerdict: HYPOTHESIS (b) CONFIRMED: batch2 paid ~19502 tokens of spike vs 36127 sequential (85% more) for identical shadowed volume.

breakEven.model: H_calls = spike / (shadowed - summary) where (shadowed - summary) tokens stop riding every subsequent prompt. Raw-token horizon and price-parameterized horizon (cacheWritePrice/cacheReadPrice as multiples of base input price) both reported.
breakEven.priceExample: at Anthropic-like pricing (write=1.25x, read=0.1x of base input): head horizon = 21282*1.25 / (3034*0.1) ~= 88 subsequent calls; middle ~= 42. Sessions shorter than the horizon LOSE money on compression under aggressive prefix caching; uncached-input providers (no prefix cache) break even in ~7 and ~3.4 raw calls respectively.
breakEven.hypothesisVerdict: HYPOTHESIS (c) CONFIRMED with a sharp edge: break-even is placement-dependent and can exceed realistic session length under cheap cache-read pricing — the nudge economy must weigh expected remaining session length, not just pressure.

engineFinding.observed: A single compress call with three disjoint ranges (each valid against the original surface, together covering all compressible turns) is rejected with "Range is entirely within the protected zone: m00007, m00008" — deterministic across two runs. The same three ranges compressed one-per-turn all succeed.
engineFinding.suspectedMechanism: later batch entries appear validated against the intermediate (post-earlier-entry) surface, where the last-5 protection window has shifted onto them
engineFinding.status: reproduced live twice; offline unit reproduction pending; kernel is pinned so an ARC-level pre-validation or sequential application may be the fix — decide after the agenda review
engineFinding.impact: the copy already encourages batching; users following it near the protected boundary hit a confusing failure
engineFinding.offlineRepro: attempted with uniform fixtures (tests/batch-compress-boundary.test.ts): batch PASSES offline — the live rejection needs an additional ingredient (snapshot-message mix, message-size asymmetry, or turn-6 instruction context). Kernel-source inspection of the protected-zone batch validation is the follow-up.

modelBehaviorFinding.observed: GLM-5.2 refused to execute an instructed compress whose provided summary asserted "no anomalies" it could not verify — correct judgment, experiment-side fix (neutral summary labels). Bench templates must not embed factual claims.
